uncited: It builds on the standard direct volume ray casting loop [19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md] by modulating the base color derived from transfer functions with a lighting term computed from local gradients [8281-lighting-and-shading-techniques.md].
The method operates within the standard direct volume ray casting framework.
For each pixel, a ray is cast through the volume, and samples are taken at regular intervals.
At each sample point $\mathbf{p}_i$, the scalar value $V(\mathbf{p}_i)$ is mapped to a base color $C_{base}$ and opacity $\alpha$ using transfer functions.
The final color contribution is modulated by a Phong lighting term $L(\mathbf{p}_i)$ calculated from the estimated surface normal.
**Sample Volume:** Iterate along the ray from the near clipping plane to the far clipping plane.
